text:
Morgan: Nightly e2e perf gate just turned red for `nightly-e2e/longseq` — p95 +42% and throughput down ~28%. CI link: https://ci.redwood/internal/job/3789
ci-bot: Job nightly-e2e/longseq #3789 failed (exit 1). Artifacts: /artifacts/3789/*.tar.gz. Summary: p95=312ms (baseline 220ms), throughput=720 rps (baseline 1000 rps).
Eli: Ack. Is this isolated to longseq or do mixedseq/nightly also show drift?
Sasha: Quick glance at the dashboard shows only longseq spike; mixedseq p95 fine. Could be a sequence-length dependent regression.
Najat: @Eli @Sasha I can spin a rerun with a longer warmup window and debug logging if that helps — will take ~15m. Want me to do it? :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Eli: Please do. Also include `--collect-kvcache-stats` and `--force-quant-profile=none` in the rerun just to rule out recent quant change. Command: `./ci/run_e2e.sh --suite longseq --warmup 120 --collect-kvcache-stats --artifact-dir /tmp/rt`
ci-bot: Rerun triggered by Najat: nightly-e2e/longseq #3790. Link: https://ci.redwood/internal/job/3790
Najat: Rerun started. Attaching quick tail of the failing step logs for context:
```
[2026-03-17 03:12:45] infer: step run_sequence len=4096 batch=8 p95=298ms
[2026-03-17 03:13:02] infer: step run_sequence len=8192 batch=4 p95=610ms
[2026-03-17 03:13:20] infer: throughput=680 rps, kvcache_hit=0.22
```
Eli: Interesting kvcache_hit is low. Could be cache invalidation change from last commit. Can we bisect to the range between yesterday's green and this red?
Sasha: I can take the bisect if you ping the suspect commit range. Last green was at `commit: a7c9f2` (yesterday 22:10), red head is `commit: b2e3d1` (this morning).
Morgan: Thanks — Sasha, could you run `./scripts/ci-bisect --start a7c9f2 --end b2e3d1 --suite longseq --quick` and post the first failing commit? If it narrows to a single PR we can revert or patch.
Sasha: On it. If the bisect is noisy I'll coordinate with Najat to attach the same warmup+kvcache flags, and ping the owners.
Morgan: Sounds good. Please @channel when we have a culprit so we can decide revert vs fix. :thumbsup:
